# D8_TRIGDEBUG_La010c3eb: vol_500 bars on the _CANC print rule + trig_trend_libstack ema_stack (10-20-50), Asia session of trading date 20261110 plus the 300 bars before it (W-D8SPEC, relay order 0037Z)

Documentation only. Series: ONE continuous series of all bars of row `vol_500` built on the D8 `_CANC` print rule (`/mnt/l2/l2vast/_d8spec/bars_c/vol_500`, 1,119,630 bars, all sessions, 2023-04 to 2026-11-13), sorted by session id then known time. Rows below: bar index 1114240 to 1114655; the Asia bars of 20261110 are idx 1114540 to 1114655 (116 bars incl. the truncated last one); 4 signals fall in this session. I recomputed the EMAs and the stack state from the stored bars and checked that my signals over the whole series equal the module's `signal_fn` output exactly (35,708 signals; equal = True).

## The bar (code: `th_bars/kernels.py k_cum` on run-merged prints; builder `runbuild.py` mode C; rule text D8_PRINT_RULE.md)
- **Threshold** = 500 x s_vol contracts, fixed for the whole trading date. s_vol = (median of the daily total volume of the previous 20 rows of the stats table) / r0, r0 = 610,702 (median of the first 60 days). For 20261110: median volume 678,505.5, **s_vol = 1.1110255, threshold = 555.5128 contracts** (the same number for all sessions of that trading date; 11-09: 549.88, 11-11: 552.82).
- **Prints:** the tape's trade records are merged into prints = consecutive records with the same price and the same aggressor side (side = last >= ask buy, last <= bid sell, from the book quote at the trade), no time condition; the merged print is added to the bar as a whole.
- **What closes the bar:** the first merged print for which the bar's cumulative volume (sum of print sizes since the bar's first print) is >= 555.5128. **The closing print stays entirely in the closing bar and the overshoot does NOT carry** to the next bar: the next bar starts empty at the next print. Overshoot (bar volume minus threshold) on this Asia session: mean 1.17, max 10.49 contracts over the 115 complete bars. The bar is **known** (`known UTC`) at the time the closing run is known to be complete = the timestamp of the next print with a different price or side (_CANC rule; the first-record stamp of _CANR is look-ahead).
- **Session reset:** the volume accumulation, and the bar series, restart at every session boundary (02:00, 08:30, 09:30, 12:00, 16:00, 18:00 ET) and at a contract change; the last bar of a session is truncated (part = 1, known at its last print; it gives no signal but stays in the series and the EMAs). Bar volume therefore varies: complete bars hold 556 to about 567 contracts.

## Indicator and event rule (code: `triggers_b/core.py`, `impl_lib.py _stack_state`, `stack_sig`)
- **EMA(n)** of the CLOSE, alpha = 2/(n+1), seeded with the first close of the whole series (2023-04-03), run over every bar of every session, no reset. Closes are back-adjusted at instrument changes by `core.prep` (column `roll adj`; **0 on every row shown**, no roll in the window; note: engine-as-run took the instrument id of each bar from the ORIGINAL vol_500 store matched on (session, bar index), see the iid note below). State carried in at the first row (idx 1114240): EMA10 = 27963.605547, EMA20 = 27965.744043, EMA50 = 27959.542197.
- **Stack state** per bar: +1 if EMA10 > EMA20 > EMA50 (both strict), -1 if EMA10 < EMA20 < EMA50, else 0.
- **Event (edge, both sides):** a bar where the state is +1 and the PREVIOUS bar's state was not +1 gives a LONG event; state -1 and previous not -1 gives a SHORT event (a bar cannot be both). It is an edge (flip INTO the stack), not a level: while the stack persists no further events. The first bar of the series and part = 1 bars give none. In the table the columns `state` and `prev state` show the test.
- **Event time** = floor(known time to whole seconds) + 2 s; session filter = Asia (sess 0). Stop/target and the flat time are those of the plain60/60 bracket and session end as described in D8_TRIGDEBUG_L7c368a4f.md (stop 60 / target 60 points, flat at 07:00 UTC = 02:00 ET, 120 s no-print exit cap).
- **iid note (engine artefact, for transparency):** `core.prep` back-adjusts older bars at changes of the instrument id, and for the _CANC vol_500 bars the id was read from the ORIGINAL (record-level) vol_500 store matched on (session id, bar index) because the frame lacked an iid column; this gives 67 adjustment steps over the series although there were only 14 real contract rolls, none in the 300+ bars shown (0 steps inside the rows, so the day's values are not affected). Re-running the stack signals with the _CANC bars' own iid changes 35 of 35,714 signals (0.1%) elsewhere in history. The effect on the book's long-run statistics is therefore negligible, but a port must back-adjust only at real rolls.

## History NT8 must carry for every value to equal the engine's (plain paragraph)
EMA10, EMA20 and EMA50 are seeded with the first close of April 2023 and never reset; the weight of the seed after N bars is (1-alpha)^N, and for EMA50 (alpha 0.0392) it is 0.1% after 175 bars and 1e-6 after 345 bars. The vol_500 series has roughly 116 bars per Asia session and about 1,300 bars per full trading day (all sessions), so starting the bar series at the beginning of the PREVIOUS trading day's Asia session (18:00 ET two days before) puts more than 1,500 bars before the first bar tested and reproduces all three EMAs to 6 digits; one trading day is enough for 4 digits. The bars themselves need: the daily threshold from the 20 previous trading dates' total volume (median / 610,702, see D8_BAR_DEFS.md section 2, a stored table of the last 60 days is in d8_testvectors/bars/_scale_inputs_last60td.csv), the bar series continuous across all sessions with a reset of the accumulation at each session boundary (02:00, 08:30, 09:30, 12:00, 16:00, 18:00 ET), the D8 print merge with the last-vs-bid/ask side (side does not change the bar boundaries of a pure volume bar but keeps the print merge exact), and the causal close stamp (next different print). Nothing else (no book, no other instrument) is used.
